subject: URGENT: Production 5xx/429 surge impacting checkout flow

Subject: URGENT: Production 5xx/429 surge impacting checkout flow

Jonas —

We're seeing an abrupt spike of 5xx and 429 responses from the Redwood hosted endpoints used in our checkout microflow. This started ~08:48 PST and is still ongoing. Error rates jumped from ~0.2% to ~12% across four pods; latency for tokenization/generation has doubled and several downstream retries are amplifying the impact.

Quick details:
- Customer impact: ~17% of checkouts failing or timing out over the last 20 minutes.
- Sample errors attached (hyperpulse-error-sample.log).
- Observed patterns: bursty 5xx with correlated increases in GPU utilization on our side; some 429s line up with autoscale events.

This is blocking a major revenue window for us. We need an immediate mitigation plan and ETA for a fix. Please escalate to infra/serving and let us know what you can do to reduce errors in the next hour.

Attaching: hyperpulse-error-sample.log

—Natalie

On Mon, Nov 15, 2027 at 09:12 AM Natalie Chang <natalie.chang@hyperpulse.com> wrote:
> We're seeing an abrupt spike of 5xx and 429 responses from the Redwood hosted endpoints used in our checkout microflow.

Initial triage notes (10:35am PST):
- Observed: the hosted pool serving the HyperPulse account is showing sustained GPU utilization ~98% across 3 nodes with request queue depth increasing. Autoscaler triggered two scale-up attempts between 08:50–09:05 but new nodes came online late (~09:15) due to cold-start + image pull retry. During that window, the runtime returned 5xx for new connections and 429s when the request expiry hit the queue limit.
- Retry amplification: client retries (short backoffs) amplified the queue; many connections retried simultaneously causing a classic retry storm.
- Correlation: increased KV cache thrashing for longer sequences, raising per-token compute cost and effective latency.

Immediate mitigations we can apply (minutes):
1) Temporarily switch HyperPulse traffic to the cheaper small-variant model (compatible, ~20% lower throughput per token but faster allocation) — manual routing override.
2) Enable burst capacity for the hosted pool (provision + warm a new spot/dedicated node) — needs platform ops to approve.
3) Reduce per-request max tokens on a best-effort basis and increase client-side jitter/backoff.
4) For customers with Dedicated pools, route to Dedicated if available (not the case for HyperPulse).

I'll start a platform action to warm an additional node and perform a routing override if we get sign-off from Marissa. Logging snippets attached and I'll push a dashboard screenshot shortly.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
SRE, Serving Runtime
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Natalie Chang <natalie.chang@hyperpulse.com>, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 10:02:18 -0800
Subject: Re: URGENT: Production 5xx/429 surge impacting checkout flow

Natalie — thanks for the heads up and apologies for the disruption. We're on this and propose the following immediate plan while Marcus warms capacity:

- 10:15 PST: temporary routing override to the small-variant model (expected to reduce allocation time and accept requests).
- 10:25 PST: enable burst capacity on the hosted pool and warm a node.
- We'll ask HyperPulse clients to apply an aggressive jittered backoff for 30 minutes (we can provide suggested retry config).

If these steps reduce error rate, we will keep the override for 1 hour and then gradually roll traffic back. If errors persist, we'll discuss a short maintenance window to drain and rebuild the pool with a newer image that contains throughput kernel fixes.

I realize this coincides with your peak — to compensate, Redwood will open a credit request (CS will send details) and prioritize a post-incident follow-up with a timeline for a durable fix (likely kernel & autoscale pacing changes).

Linking to the dashboard screenshot: redwood-dashboard-screenshot.png
Attaching our mitigation note: ma-recommendation-note.pdf

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

—Natalie
